turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He couldn't help but feel a bit overwhelmed by Miss Havisham's manner, and he was worried about Estella's presence making things even more awkward, so he ventured to explain that he was very sorry, but his sister, Magwitch, was very unwell and he had promised to stay with her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes, red-rimmed and sunken, seemed to bore into Pip's very soul as she spoke, her voice dripping with disdain. Foolish boy, his sister's health was of no consequence here, and he would play with Estella, as he was instructed. The cold, mirthless smile that played on her lips made Pip shudder, and he felt a sense of foreboding wash over him as he reluctantly rose to join Estella in the adjacent room.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He hoped, Miss Havisham, that his sister's condition might be taken into consideration, and that he might be allowed to return home, as his mother was in a great state about it.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, to think that a mere sister's illness could absolve him from his duties here, when Estella's education is at stake!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He didn't think it was right to play with Estella when his sister was so poorly, and he hoped Miss Havisham might understand that he couldn't possibly stay away from home for long.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes blazed with indignation as she spoke, her voice like a rusty gate, 'How dare you question my authority, boy! You will play with Estella, and you will do it with a smile, lest you forfeit any claim to my favor or your sister's well-being.'

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He didn't know how he could play with Estella when his sister was so poorly, and it seemed to him that Miss Havisham didn't understand the worry he felt for her

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, to think that a sister's illness could possibly rival the importance of Estella's education, or that he could abandon his duties here at a whim!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Perhaps, Miss Havisham, it would be better if he stayed with his sister, for she is very poorly and needs him at home

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, to think that a sister's illness could possibly rival the importance of Estella's education, or that he could abandon his duties here at a whim!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He didn't know how he could leave his sister, Miss Havisham, and he was afraid it would be wrong to abandon her at such a time

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, to think that family obligations can be allowed to interfere with a greater purpose, Estella's education will not wait for your sister's convalescence!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He didn't know what to make of Miss Havisham's stern words, but he felt a great sense of unease, and he wished he might be excused from his duties here, to return to his sister's bedside

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, to think that a sister's illness could possibly compare to the sacrifices that must be made for Estella's future, she will not be swayed by such petty concerns!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He didn't wish to be a trouble to Miss Havisham, but he truly couldn't leave his sister in such a state

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, to think that family obligations can be set aside for the sake of sentimental attachments, Estella's education will not be delayed by your sentimental weakness!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: He felt rather overcome, he explained, and if Miss Havisham would be so kind as to excuse him, he would be most grateful to take his leave and attend to his sister's needs at once

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, to think that a sister's illness could possibly compare to the sacrifices that must be made for Estella's future, she will not be swayed by such petty concerns!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Miss Havisham was being very hard, he thought, and he didn't know how he could ask her to understand, but he felt that he had to try, for his sister's sake

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, to think that the sacrifices made for Estella's future are not already being repaid, in full measure, by the education and refinement she will bring to some worthy husband, and it is not as if you are a martyr, Pip, merely a weak-willed boy who cannot even manage his own affairs.

opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born.
